text.p: Major Danish shipping, oil and gas group A.P. Moeller announced on Thursday a rise in 1996 group profits over 1996 and said that it expected 1997 to show further improved profits in its shipping business.
The group announced 1996 net profit of 2.2 billion crowns compared to 1.8 billion the year before, and said that pre-tax profits were up to 3.5 billion crowns from 2.8 billion in 1995.
"Shipping activities for the time being indicate a 1997 result better than that of 1996," its annual report said.
The group increased turnover to 33 billion crowns in 1996, from 28 billion the year before.
It increased short-term borrowing to 7.6 billion crowns from 6.0 billion in 1995 while long-term debt was little changed, at 11.9 billion in 1996 from 11.7 the previous year.

Its Maersk oil and gas unit made a profit of 279 billion crowns after a loss of 103 million in 1995, but airline Maersk Air's earnings fell to 119 million crowns from a previous 202 million, despite a 400 million crown rise.
